rows.grounds: relative pronoun referring to the reciter
state of complete union with brahman

items.question: What spiritual attainment results from reciting with focused intent?
premises: A person becomes intent-focused before reciting.
Such a person may recite the text.
Recitation with focus leads to union with brahman.
items.inference: Therefore, the focused reciter may attain union with brahman.
items.plain_english: Whoever, having become intent and focused, recites this may attain union with Brahman.

rows.grounds: causative act of making others hear
recipients who are one's own relatives

items.question: Whom should the wise person teach and make hear this teaching?
premises: A wise person may cause others to hear the teaching.
A wise person may cause others to understand it.
The intended recipients are one's own kinsmen steadfast in brahman.
items.inference: Therefore, the wise person should teach and explain this to kinsmen devoted to brahman.
items.plain_english: The wise one may cause his own kinsmen, who are steadfast in Brahman, to hear and understand it.

rows.grounds: cause arising from holding in memory

items.question: What certain result follows from recitation and retention of this teaching?
premises: Recitation can produce a transformative effect.
Retention in memory can produce a transformative effect.
Through these, one becomes a knower of brahman.
items.inference: Therefore, recitation and retention certainly give rise to knowledge of brahman.
items.plain_english: From recitation and retention of it, one certainly becomes a knower of Brahman.

items.question: Which divine protectors are invoked to guard the throat and face?
premises: The throat is to be protected by the world-protector.
The face is to be protected by the all-seer.
The all-pervading one is invoked as protector.
items.inference: Therefore, specific divine aspects are called upon to protect specific body parts.
items.plain_english: May the protector of the world protect the throat; may the all-seeing, all-pervading one protect the face.

rows.grounds: the entire body as object of protection

items.question: What divine principle is asked to protect the entire body at all times?
premises: Protection is sought for all limbs.
Protection is sought at all times.
The protector invoked is the supreme eternal brahman.
items.inference: Therefore, the supreme eternal brahman is invoked to protect the whole body always.
items.plain_english: May the supreme, eternal Brahman always protect all the limbs.

rows.grounds: that which has become the support of the world
devoid of any refuge or basis

items.question: How can the ultimate reality be both the world's support and without support?
premises: The reality is described as the support of the world.
The same reality is described as without support.
The same reality is described as devoid of any refuge.
items.inference: Therefore, the ultimate reality supports all while itself depending on nothing.
uncertainties: The grammatical object of these epithets is implied from context, possibly brahman or the hymn's object.
items.plain_english: It is the support of the world, yet itself without support and devoid of any refuge.

rows.grounds: name or designation of the hymn
indicates the opening formula of the text

items.question: In what state must one recite the hymn beginning with the five jewels?
premises: The hymn is identified as beginning with 'five jewels'.
The reciter must be intent-focused.
The reciter must be pure.
items.inference: Therefore, this hymn must be recited by one who is focused and pure.
items.plain_english: This hymn, beginning with 'the five jewels', should be recited by one who is intent, focused, and pure.

rows.grounds: marks the end of the quoted or concluded statement

items.question: What does the text commence to declare after stating the recitation obligation?
premises: The hymn is declared to be recited.
Therefore a further declaration is introduced.
The text commences to declare that matter.
items.inference: Therefore, having stated the obligation, the text begins its formal declaration.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'that' (tat) depends on the following context.
items.plain_english: It is to be recited; therefore, the text now commences to declare that, thus.

rows.grounds: designation of the nature as consciousness

items.question: What essential nature is attributed to the subject in this designation?
premises: The subject is described by a single epithet.
The epithet identifies its form as consciousness.
This presents consciousness as its essential nature.
items.inference: Therefore, the subject is characterized as having the nature of consciousness.
uncertainties: The subject of this epithet is not explicitly stated in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Whose form is consciousness.

rows.grounds: purpose of attaining the fruits of the four human goals
ritual or formal application of the text

items.question: For what purpose is the formal application of this text proclaimed?
premises: A formal application of the text is proclaimed.
The application aims at attaining fruits.
Those fruits are the four goals of human life.
items.inference: Therefore, the text's application is proclaimed for attaining the four human goals.
items.plain_english: Its application is proclaimed for the attainment of the fruits of the four goals of life.

rows.grounds: state of being wholly composed of brahman

items.question: What transformation occurs upon directly attaining knowledge of brahman?
premises: One may directly attain knowledge of brahman.
Such attainment is immediate and direct.
This attainment results in becoming full of brahman.
items.inference: Therefore, direct knowledge of brahman makes one become brahman-full.
items.plain_english: Having directly attained knowledge of Brahman, he may become wholly full of Brahman.

rows.grounds: alternative location for wearing or placing
resulting status of mastery over all powers

items.question: What mastery is gained by bearing this on the throat or right arm?
premises: The text may be borne on the throat.

Bearing it leads to lordship over all perfections.
items.inference: Therefore, wearing this on the throat or right arm may confer mastery over all perfections.
uncertainties: The object borne (e.g. the hymn as amulet) is implied from context.
items.plain_english: Worn on the throat or on the right arm, one may become lord of all perfections.

rows.grounds: qualified recipient who is a disciple

items.question: To what kind of recipient should this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given to a beloved pupil.
The recipient should be devoted to the guru.
The recipient should be intelligent.
items.inference: Therefore, this teaching should be transmitted only to a devoted and discerning pupil.
items.plain_english: One may give it to a beloved, intelligent pupil who is devoted to the guru.

rows.grounds: the hymn functioning as protective armor

items.question: What should the foremost practitioner do after reciting the hymn-armor?
premises: The foremost practitioner recites the hymn-armor.
Recitation is completed before the next act.
The next act is reverential prostration.
items.inference: Therefore, after reciting the hymn-armor, the foremost practitioner should prostrate.
items.plain_english: Having recited the hymn-armor, the foremost practitioner should prostrate.

rows.grounds: salutation to the one without qualities
salutation to the one whose form is being

items.question: What aspects of the divine are honored in this repeated salutation?
premises: Salutation is offered to the qualityless one.
Salutation is offered to the one of true form.
Obeisance is repeated for emphasis.
items.inference: Therefore, the salutation honors both the qualityless and true-form aspects of the divine.
items.plain_english: Obeisance to you, the qualityless one; obeisance, obeisance to you, whose form is true being.

items.question: What inner condition is required in the worship of the supreme lord?
premises: Worship is directed to the supreme lord.
Worship involves an inner condition.
That inner condition is purity of mind.
items.inference: Therefore, purity of mind is accomplished or required in worship of the supreme lord.
items.plain_english: In the worship of the supreme Lord, purity of mind is accomplished.

items.question: What sacred offering from brahman should the practitioner accept?
premises: There is a great grace or consecrated offering.
It comes from brahman, the supreme self.
The practitioner should accept it.
items.inference: Therefore, one should accept the great grace of brahman, the supreme self.
items.plain_english: One should accept the great grace of Brahman, the supreme Self.

items.question: Where and when should the practice directed toward brahman be performed?
premises: The practice directed toward brahman should be accomplished.
It should be done in all places.
It should be done at all times.
items.inference: Therefore, brahman-sadhana should be practiced everywhere and at all times.
items.plain_english: One should practice the discipline of Brahman in all places and at all times.

rows.grounds: required inner state of the worshipper

items.question: How should one with a pure mind worship the supreme self?
premises: The supreme self is the object of worship.
The worshipper should be pure-minded.
Worship should be performed always.
items.inference: Therefore, the pure-minded person should always worship the supreme self.
items.plain_english: With a pure mind, one should always worship the supreme Self.

items.question: What quality belongs to that which is offered to the supreme lord?
premises: Something is offered to the supreme lord.
That offering alone is singled out.
It is described as greatly purifying.
items.inference: Therefore, what is offered to the supreme lord is itself greatly purifying.
items.plain_english: Whatever is offered to the supreme Lord, that alone is greatly purifying.

rows.grounds: assertion of non-existence of the distinction

items.question: Does ritual purity distinction apply to an offering dedicated to supreme brahman?
premises: An offering may be dedicated to supreme brahman.
Ordinarily distinctions of touched and untouched apply.
In such a dedicated offering this distinction does not exist.
items.inference: Therefore, offerings dedicated to supreme brahman transcend the touched-untouched distinction.
items.plain_english: In a substance offered to the supreme Brahman, there is no distinction of touched and untouched.

items.inference: Therefore, in this context, purity of mind means purity of the inner organ.
uncertainties: This verse reads as a gloss or commentary fragment rather than a complete sentence.
items.plain_english: Beginning with 'worship' and so on: purity of mind means purity of the inner organ.

uncertainties: The action or predicate governing this locative is supplied by surrounding verses.
items.plain_english: In a śālagrāma stone and the like.

items.question: How should the practitioner partake of food after dedicating it to brahman?
premises: The practitioner dedicates the food to brahman.
After dedication, the practitioner may eat.
The meal may be taken together with one's own people.
items.inference: Therefore, after offering food to brahman, the practitioner may eat it with family or kin.
items.plain_english: Having dedicated it to Brahman, the practitioner may eat together with his own people.
